dedupe_keys.name: kariba dam rehabilitation project plunge pool reshaping to protect the dam from scour

description: The Zambezi River Authority reports on rehabilitating the 128 metre high, 716 metre long Kariba arch dam on the Zambia and Zimbabwe border, a 60-year-old structure whose repair budget is US$294 million. Repeated spillway operation scoured an 80 metre deep plunge pool downstream, and the plunge pool reshaping sub-project, financed by an EU grant with Gruner Stucky as engineer and Razel-Bec as contractor from May 2017, widens and reshapes it to cut the force of the jets. By December 2023 excavation of about 300,100 cubic metres of rock, with 20,000 square metres of slopes anchored and shotcreted, was complete, 550,000 cubic metres of water had been pumped out, the overall project was 93 percent complete, and a reinforced concrete slab over the weak rock zone and re-watering were the last steps. Coverage: one dam. Access: free press releases; the licence is not stated. Caveats: an owner's progress reports without the underlying model results. It supports dam scour, spillway and rehabilitation planning studies, and relates to the ZRA Kariba lake level data and the Toddbrook spillway failure case study in the catalogue.
